_policy: Accepted high/critical dependency advisories, checked by scripts/audit-check.mjs.
An entry is a maintainer decision, not a note: everything not listed here fails the
Security workflow. Keep them narrow (one advisory, one package, one tree), give a
reason that names the shipped or reachable path, and set an expiry so the call is
re-made rather than inherited. Past the expiry date the build fails until the entry
is removed or renewed. Prefer upgrading: a version bump deletes the entry.
Trees: "." is the Electron app, "website" is the isolated docs sub-project.

exceptions.reason: Build-time devDependency, and the flagged copy is unreachable for the targets this project builds. electron-builder 26.15.3 pulls electron-builder-squirrel-windows 25.1.8, which carries its own app-builder-lib 25.1.8; that path is only entered for the squirrel-windows target, and package.json sets build.win.target to nsis. The AppImage LD_LIBRARY_PATH defect the advisory describes is fixed in 26.15.0, and our AppImage is produced by the top-level app-builder-lib 26.15.3 (pnpm-lock.yaml). Overriding the nested copy to 26.x cannot be verified without a full Windows packaging run, so this waits on electron-builder bumping its squirrel dependency.

Same unreachable squirrel-windows chain as GHSA-7g7r-gx96-252g. The advisory is about electron-updater leaking credential headers across a redirect; the shipped electron-updater 6.8.9 resolves builder-util-runtime 9.7.0, which is patched (pnpm-lock.yaml), and no vulnerable copy ships in the app.

Docs-site build dependency only; nothing from website/ ships in the app or runs on a server. The libvips CVEs need untrusted image input, and next.config.mjs sets images.unoptimized with output: export, so Next never invokes sharp. Fixing means bumping next in the isolated website tree, which needs a site build to verify and is not covered by this repo's verify loop.

Docs-site build dependency only. The attack needs attacker-controlled CSS carrying a sourceMappingURL comment; the site's CSS is repo-authored (website/app + Tailwind). Next pins postcss to an exact version, so an override is a compatibility risk that belongs in a website-only change with a site build behind it.
Same dependency, path and reasoning as GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q — a second sourceMappingURL traversal advisory against the same pinned postcss.

Reached only through serve, the local static preview (website `pnpm start`). It is not used by `next build`, not installed on the Pages runner path that publishes the site, and never processes third-party requests. Fixable by an override in website/pnpm-workspace.yaml, which requires regenerating the isolated website lockfile.
Same local-preview-only path as GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7. The DoS needs an attacker-supplied glob; the patterns come from serve's own configuration. Fixable by the same website-lockfile change.
